extracted.intended_audience: medical journal editors, authors, peer reviewers, and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Authoritative recommendations from the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors covering roles/responsibilities, editorial/publishing issues, manuscript preparation/submission, and use of AI in medical journal publishing. Intended to guide journals, editors, authors, and reviewers on ethical and procedural standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of the purpose of the ICMJE Recommendations (why the recommendations exist and what they aim to achieve).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Should Use the Recommendations?
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of the intended users of the Recommendations (which stakeholders—authors, editors, journals, institutions—should apply them).

rubrics_metrics.name: History of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Background and development history of the ICMJE Recommendations (context for their evolution and prior iterations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining the Role of Authors and Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for defining authorship and contributions (who qualifies as an author, contributor roles, and responsibilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Financial and Non-Financial Relationships and Activities, and Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for disclosure of financial and non‑financial relationships and activities that could constitute conflicts of interest for authors, reviewers, or editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities in the Submission and Peer-Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations and duties of authors, reviewers, and editors during submission and peer review (timeliness, confidentiality, fairness, transparency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Owners and Editorial Freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on relationships between journal owners and editorial independence, protecting editorial freedom from undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Research Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards to ensure the protection of human research participants, including ethical oversight, consent, and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and Version Control
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on issuing corrections, retractions, expressions of concern, and managing versions of published content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and procedures for handling scientific misconduct (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism) and related investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on copyright ownership, licensing, and transfer for articles and related materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards addressing redundant, duplicate, or overlapping publications and expectations for transparency and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for letters to the editor, author responses, and other correspondence related to published material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on fees related to publication (page charges, APCs, submission fees) and disclosure of such arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplements, Theme Issues, and Special Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for publishing sponsored supplements, themed issues, or special series and handling sponsorship/editorial control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorships and Partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and transparency expectations for journal sponsorships, partnerships, and other financial relationships that may affect content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on electronic publishing practices, online content management, and related ethical/technical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing advertising in journals and separation of advertising from editorial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals and the Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on interactions between journals/authors and the media, including press releases and accurate representation of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and guidance related to clinical trial reporting, registration, and data-sharing expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a Manuscript for Submission to a Medical Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions and standards for preparing manuscripts for submission, including format, ethical declarations, and reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending the Manuscript to the Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural guidance for submitting manuscripts to journals (cover letters, submission systems, required forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and standards for authors' use of artificial intelligence tools in preparing manuscripts (disclosure, acceptable uses, limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reviewers' use of AI in the peer-review process (confidentiality, reliability, disclosure obligations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' Role in Ensuring Responsible Use of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for editors to oversee and ensure responsible, transparent use of AI in manuscript preparation and review.
